Ai, let me think about this year on my 7 mu...

I'm 50 now, been on this land 35 years. Just me and the wife at home — kids are grown, working in town, don't come back except for New Year. So we're the only hands. Can't do too much heavy work like before, my back isn't what it was.

Same plan as most years, because it works. Chili is where the money is, but it's a lot of work — picking, picking, picking all summer. So I'll do about 3 mu of chili, then cabbage on the same 3 mu after the chili finishes in August. That's my chili-cabbage, same as the village does.

Maize on another 3 mu — not as much money but it's easy, and we keep some to eat and some to sell. No wheat before it, I stopped doing wheat years ago, too much work for what you get. So spring maize, plant end of April when the ground warms up.

The last 1 mu I put in spinach in the autumn, lets it sit through winter and cut in early spring. Mostly for us to eat, sell a bit at the village market. Easy crop, doesn't need much.

Chili seedlings I buy from old Wang's nursery like always, around 300 yuan per mu worth. Before I put them in I spread a bag of compound fertilizer per mu and some chicken manure from my cousin — he gives it cheap. When they start flowering I topdress about half a bag of urea per mu. My neighbor Li puts more but I can't afford that every year, and my chili still does okay. Spray for aphids and those little flies three or four times, the shop in town tells me what to buy.

Cabbage after chili, the soil is still good from the chili fertilizer so I just put one bag of compound and a bit of urea when it heads up. Water 3-4 times, watch for bugs.

Maize — hybrid seed, buy new every year, saved seed doesn't grow right. Compound at planting, urea when it's about knee-high. Water maybe twice if no rain. Spray herbicide early so I don't have to weed by hand, my back can't do that anymore.

Spinach is cheap and easy. Little seed, little fertilizer. Water once or twice.

Money — all told maybe 4000-some yuan in inputs. That's about what I can manage. If chili price is good this year I'll do okay, if not, well, we have the maize and spinach to eat at least.
